# Basic mathematics

Mathematics is the foundation of all quantitative methods. And since this is whole book is about quantitative methods, it is natural to begin with the foundation. A certain group of reader might want to skip this section or part of it and only return to specific chapters when notation and concept issues in later chapter are unclear.

The usefuleness of mathematics has become a low hanging fruit for humorists (does knowing the square root of 25 has saved you in difficult situtation?). Math phobia^[an intense, persistent feeling of tension, apprehension, or fear that interferes with a person's ability to manipulate numbers and solve math problems in daily life or academic settings] is real, and many relates to these jokes.

Unconciously, validate the difficulty and uselessness of mathematics. But math can be
  - easy and useful in everyday life like arithmetic operation
  - difficult and useless like proving Fermat's last theorem
  - difficult and usefull like partial differential equations
  - easy and useless like calculating $\pi = 3.14...$ up to any precision.
The idea behind this section is to wander in the easy and useful part. Easy in the sense of simplified and useful for applied ecologist and scientist-alike.

Most chapters are to support future applied concept. The first chapters remind of the different rules in arithmetic (@sec-arithmeticMath), what are the greek letters and why are they used (@sec-greek). The difference between discrete and continuous variables (@sec-discreteContinuous) which will be used in the statistics and coding section. The notation for summation for product are explained in (@sec-sum). These compact notations will be used throughtout in the define many statistics. Matrix and operations on matrix are covered in three chapters (@sec-matrixMath, @sec-matrixOperationMath, and @sec-matrixMultiplicationMath).

The rest of this section redefines what is function with an emphasis on the notion of domain and codomain (@sec-functionMath), the interpretations of a graph (@sec-functionViz) and the derivative (@sec-derivative). The exponential and logarithm functions are introduced (@sec-exponential and @sec-log). The section ends with the formulation of how to model change with difference (@sec-difference) or differential equation (@sec-differential)

This section is about basic mathematics so there is no a priori use of R code. Coding are introduced in the respective section. Mathematicians might protest against the narrow definition and intuition, the goal is to find a trade-off where reduced rigor might make concept more accessible.
